answers.explanation: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and cellular are all uses of radio waves.
That's why low-frequency AM radio crosses states, and infrared can't get past your hand.
The antenna turns electrical signals into radio waves and back.
Microwaves sit at the high end of that range, from 1 to 300 GHz.
Every other transmitter on a nearby frequency is noise, and storms can disrupt the signal too.
There's only one airwave. Everyone nearby on the same frequency shares it.
With a cable, an attacker has to get at the cable. With radio, standing in the parking lot is enough.
Listening to radio doesn't transmit anything, so passive eavesdropping is invisible.
Encryption, like WPA3 for Wi-Fi, makes the captured signal useless to the listener.
